name: Real-website re-run 2: the relay's downstream clock (client-only clock vs both directions clocked)
code: main at bf80b62 (cloak protocol v2) with the lab-only AVPN_WIRE_CLOCK_DOWNSTREAM switch; run rerun2b-20261116 (~/vm/advanced-vpn/wf-real/rerun2.sh)

variants.clockup: fast + the client's wire clock only (AVPN_WIRE_CLOCK_DOWNSTREAM=0): the first re-run's 'clock'
variants.clockboth: fast + the wire clock on the client and the relay

setup.rounds: 5 interleaved rounds x 3 variants x 20 sites x 2 loads = 600 loads, same day, same sites
setup.cpu: browser and client data plane share cores 0,1 (the busy-CPU case); relay, exit and capture on 2,3; on mains power
setup.attack: k-FP closed world, 20 sites, chance 5% (tools/wf_deep.py); per direction against 100 shuffled-label runs (tools/wf_residual.py)
setup.note: A first attempt the same day failed: another job exhausted memory, the lab froze 6.2 h and its network never recovered (13 of 40 loads); discarded. This run had that job paused.

findings: Undefended k-FP 90.5%: the attack works on this collection.
Client-only clock: 10.4% (p = 0.030 over 100 shuffled-label runs), replicating the first re-run's 9.5% (p = 0.048). A residual leak under the client-only clock is established across two runs.
Both directions clocked: 5.15%, equal to the shuffled-label mean (p = 0.58). The full k-FP attack finds nothing.

Per direction, the client-only clock's residual sat in the upstream here (8.8%, p = 0.040; downstream 5.2%, p = 0.49), the opposite of the first re-run (downstream p = 0.0099, upstream p = 0.079). Its location is not stable across runs; the earlier statement that it is in the downstream over-read one run.

With both clocked, downstream packets alone still score 9.3% (p = 0.030; about 0.09 corrected for the three views), while the full attack is at chance. A weak downstream signal may remain; more loads are needed to settle it.
Cost of the relay clock over the client-only clock: page-load success 93.0% vs 96.5% (the extra failures are TikTok and Netflix timing out at 30 s) and median load 8.9 s vs 8.1 s (undefended 6.2 s).
status: The relay's clock brings the full real-website attack to chance at a modest cost. Not yet a default: one 20-site closed world on one machine and network, a possible weak downstream signal, and the heavy-site timeouts.
next: More loads per site (and open world) to settle the downstream-only signal.
Look at the heavy-site timeouts: the clock's rate against the site's demand.
